text:
Sasha: Heads-up — started a 5% canary for model v5-quant4 on /generate around the long-doc workload. Quick smoke shows hallucination rate up vs v4 baseline on the >2k token slice. Posting raw deltas.
Kevin: Thanks. can you paste the slice breakdown?
Sasha: sure, quick dump:
```
slice: long-doc (>2000 tokens)
  baseline(v4): hallucination_rate=4.1%, mrr=0.842, p99_latency=220ms
  v5-quant4:   hallucination_rate=7.3% (+3.2pp), mrr=0.831 (-0.011), p99=235ms (+15ms)
slice: short (<200 tokens)
  baseline: hallucination_rate=1.0%, mrr=0.912
  v5-quant4: hallucination_rate=1.1% (+0.1pp), mrr=0.913 (+0.001)
overall token cost: v5-quant4 ~ -18% per-token CPU
```
Lina: ugh long-doc jump is noticeable. Is hallucination defined like the eval spec (factuality PR-AU)?
Sasha: yes same eval harness we use for onboard checks — mix of synthetic QA + human-labeled anchor set.
Ana: Our auto-fallback threshold is currently configured to trigger when core slices see >2.0pp uplift in hallucination OR relative MRR drop >1.0%. This would trip on the long-doc slice alone.
Ryan: Do we know if this is a distributional effect from kv-cache behavior after quantization? Any logs from the runtime? @DeployBot, did the rollout hit the same hardware profile as the baseline shadow run?
DeployBot: Canary rollout started 1711135790: 5% traffic -> nodes in pool "dedicated-q3" (A100s mixed), same routing config as baseline. No runtime OOMs. Observability job "onboard-evals-longdoc" scheduled.
Kevin: Could it be seqlen-dependent kernel path? v5 changes attention fuse ordering and that can interact with int4 kernels. Suggest: reduce canary to 1% and run extended shadow on long-docs with deterministic seeds.
Sasha: Agree. Proposal: pause promotion, dial traffic from 5% -> 1% immediately; launch targeted eval run (50k long-doc queries, seeded) and run diffs for hallucination taxonomy + MRR per prompt class. Also add a delta-agg on kv-cache hit rate.
Ana: +1. Also set the auto-fallback to immediate fallback for the long-doc slice (route to v4) until we have the deeper analysis — we can keep shadowing v5-quant4 to collect more traces.
Lina: I'll prepare the eval harness and include the new hallucination severity buckets (minor/major/critical). Will also add a synthetic worst-case where we prepend a noisy prefix to trigger cache churning.
Ryan: If it's quantization-triggered, check weight-permute differences during post-quantize step. Also run a quick un-quantized v5 build (float16) as sanity — if float16 aligns with baseline, it's a quant interaction.
Sasha: timeline: do the 1% throttle now (canary rollback path set to automatic if metrics worsen further). Expect preliminary evals in 3 hours, full run overnight.
Kevin: For the record, let's add the automatic fallback thresholds we used here to the rollout config: long-doc hallucination delta >= 2.0pp -> immediate reroute; any MRR drop >= 1.0% on core slices -> hold and notify eng-ml.
Ana: I'll flip the routing rule and start the shadow job.
Sasha: Thanks. I'll post the eval job link when ready and tag folks. :eyes:
Lina: ping me once the seed corpus is uploaded, I'll run the severity breakdown.
Ryan: Great. If we confirm it's quant noise, plan B: try per-layer mixed-quant schedule (leave attention/query/proj layers higher precision) before we consider promoting.
Sasha: Ok locking the action: 1) throttle to 1% now; 2) start focused seed eval; 3) route long-doc slice to v4 via temporary pin; 4) investigate quant-layer mix. Will update thread with links.
DeployBot: Canary traffic change executed at 1711135810: 5% -> 1%. Routing rule applied: long-doc slice pinned to v4.
Ana: :thumbsup: keep us posted.
Sasha: Will do — thanks all.
